definitions.explanation: A pattern of squares of two alternating colors, like a chessboard. Used on kimono cloth, floor tiles, wrapping paper, and design work generally.

examples.japanese: {市松模様|いちまつもよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧。
{市松模様|いちまつもよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}た→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦{女性|じょせい}→女性：01617_josei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{歩|ある}いていた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: A woman in a checkered kimono was walking by.

examples.japanese: ⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦オリンピック→オリンピック：09899_orinpikku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧エンブレム⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{藍色|あいいろ}→藍色：15519_aiiro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{市松模様|いちまつもよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われ→使う：00473_tsukau⟧、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦らしい→らしい：09502_rashii⟧⟦{意匠|いしょう}→意匠：12689_ishou⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧になった。
examples.english: The Tokyo Olympics emblem used an indigo checkerboard pattern, and it drew attention as a distinctly Japanese design.

notes:
Formed from {市松|いちまつ} + ⟦{模様|もよう}→模様：03635_moyou⟧ (pattern). The name comes from the Edo-period kabuki actor Sanogawa Ichimatsu, who wore hakama in this pattern on stage and made it fashionable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {市松模様|いちまつもよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{布|ぬの}→布：01489_nuno⟧: checkered cloth
- {市松模様|いちまつもよう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧: to arrange in a checkerboard pattern
- ⟦{白黒|しろくろ}→白黒：13642_shirokuro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{市松模様|いちまつもよう}: a black-and-white checkerboard pattern

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦チェック→チェック：03000_chekku⟧: check, plaid — the loanword, used mainly for woven cloth patterns with crossing lines
- ⟦{縞模様|しまもよう}→縞模様：26237_shimamoyou⟧: stripe pattern — parallel lines rather than alternating squares
